newsitem.title: USA: Dataquest sees DRAM oversupply lessening in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Dataquest sees DRAM oversupply lessening in 1997.

text.p: The worldwide dynamic random access memory, or DRAM, market is showing signs of rebounding from last year's oversupply, Dataquest Inc said Tuesday, but the research firm said balanced supply and demand will not come together this year.
Dataquest said the DRAM oversupply rate will likely run at seven percent per quarter for most of 1997, down from the more than 10 percent oversupply the market experienced in the first half of 1996.
DRAM suppliers must remain wary that any unexpected near-term weakening of demand, which has been strong and growing, could return the market to 1996 conditions, Dataquest said.

Dataquest said its analysts expect the PC market to proceed with positive growth in 1997, which bodes well for the DRAM market. The research firm said the personal computer industry is the largest consumer of DRAMs, so much of the DRAM market's success is based on the continued growth in the PC market.
Production cutbacks by South Korean suppliers have become a DRAM supply-side "wild card," Dataquest said.
